title: Hobbies
text:
Surfing






My hometown break








Surfing is a big part of the culture of Half Moon Bay, where I grew up. I’m blessed enough to be able to partake in it and have been surfing for years.


Hiking










Nature has always been a big part of my life, and hiking has been a great way for me to spend more time within it. Trails that incorporate scrambling across boulders and rock faces are my favorite.


Cooking


















Cooking is one of my favorite hobbies, and I would like to consider it a talent. I love preparing food for my friends and family, I love experimenting and eyeballing, and I’ve found a lot of success with both. I am working on my presentation skills, but I think I have the flavor and texture down for many dishes.

title: About Me
text:
Hometown - Half Moon Bay, CA






Map 1. The location of Half Moon Bay on a map of California.
I’m from a small town about thirty minutes south of San Francisco called Half Moon Bay. It is a truly beautiful place as it is nestled between the Pacific Ocean on one side and the Santa Cruz mountains on the other side, similar to how it is here in Santa Barbara. Growing up there cemented my love for the outdoors, especially the mountains and the sea.


Education
I graduated from the University of California Santa Barbara in the Spring of 2026 with Bachelor’s of Science in Environmental Studies. Of the subjects I studied, ecology is the subject I’ve found most interesting. I specifically enjoy topics like ecological restoration and management, as well as community ecology, plant ecology, and fire ecology. Additionally, I liked learning how to use tools like RStudio and ArcGIS Pro to help analyze and visualize data within these fields.


Favorite Plants
Over the past few years, I’ve really grown to appreciate the plants around me. I’ve always liked plants, but I enjoy being in there company more now. I also have a few local favorites.

1. Juncus bufonius - Common toad rush





I love their rusty colored flowers, especially during the drier parts of the year when they begin to pop more due to the color contrast with the rest of their structure.


2. Centromadia parryi ssp. australis - Southern tarplant





I like how spiky tarplant is and its small yellow flowers. Also a California Rare Plant Rank: 1B.1 which I find pretty neat considering we have them on campus. Took this photo on 05/28/2025!


3. Artemesia californica - California sagebrush





I’m a big fan of the smell of sagebrush. It’s always a treat to run my hands through one to get smell their herbaceous scent.

title: Elias Dewald
text: Hello! My name is Eli and I’m a recent 2026 Environmental Studies graduate from the University of California Santa Barbara and a Lab Assistant for the UCSB Cheadle Center for Biodiversity and Ecological Restoration. I enjoy doing restoration work, working with plants, and learning more about the field of restoration and how to share my interest in it. Outside of work, I love surfing, hiking, cooking, socializing, and again, plants. Check out the rest of my website to learn more about me!
